title: Symphony No. 4 / Nocturnes
description: The orchestra's first stereo session, recorded over three cold evenings in a hall that has since been demolished. Still the reference version for the Nocturnes as far as most of our customers are concerned.
label: Harrow Lane Records

title: Music for Strings and Winter
description: A programme of short pieces assembled almost as an afterthought and now the most requested record in the orchestra's catalogue. Restrained playing, beautifully captured.
label: Harrow Lane Records

title: Evensong at St Brendan's
description: Recorded in the church itself with two microphones and no acoustic treatment whatsoever. The building does at least half the work and nobody involved pretended otherwise.
label: Lantern Row

title: Blue Hour
description: The session that named the band, cut in a single night after a fortnight of club dates. You can hear the fatigue, and it improves everything.
label: Meridian Tapes

title: Second Set
description: Looser and warmer than the debut, with two of the longest tracks the group ever committed to tape. The rhythm section is the whole story here.
label: Meridian Tapes

title: Three Sides of the Room
description: A debut with nothing to prove and no interest in proving it anyway. Piano, bass and drums arranged as a conversation rather than a hierarchy.
label: Blue Meridian

title: Quiet Arithmetic
description: The trio at their most severe and their most rewarding, working through a set of originals built on very small ideas. Repays close attention.
label: Blue Meridian

title: Hard Country Lines
description: Recorded in a radio station after hours because it was the only room available with a working microphone. One man, one guitar, no second takes.
label: Foundry Street

title: Trouble the Water
description: The record that got him heard outside the county, collecting sides cut across four years and three states. The tape hiss is part of the deal.
label: Foundry Street

title: Bailando en la Azotea
description: A full orchestra recorded live in a ballroom, with the percussion mixed exactly where a dancer would want it. Nothing about this record is for sitting down.
label: Coastal Union

title: Tarde de Vidro
description: Bossa arrangements stripped back until only the voice and the guitar are load-bearing. Her best-known record and deservedly so.
label: Verdant Sound

title: After the Curtain Falls
description: The in-film recordings from a 1963 picture, released as a straight album because the studio thought it would sell. It did not, and then forty years later it very much did.
label: Gable End

title: Sweetheart Frequency
description: The crossover record, built from country songs given orchestral arrangements nobody expected to work. They worked.
label: Nightpost Records

title: Boone Sings the Standards
description: Recorded in four days with a band who had clearly done this before. A covers record that earns its place through phrasing alone.
label: Nightpost Records

title: Furnace Road
description: Recorded in eleven days in a converted garage with the amps facing the wall. Loud, mean and entirely without pretension.
label: Ash & Iron Records

title: Steel and Sundown
description: The one where the songs caught up with the volume. Still their biggest seller and the obvious place to start.
label: Ash & Iron Records

title: The Long Shift
description: Cut in the gaps between a punishing touring schedule, which is why it sounds like a band rather than a project. Grooves first, everything else after.
label: Trestle Records

title: Parade Ground
description: Their most ambitious record, arranged for a slightly larger group and better for it. The closing track runs to fourteen minutes and earns every one.
label: Trestle Records

title: Timber and Tin
description: One room, one microphone, five players standing in a circle. The old method, used because it is the right one rather than out of nostalgia.
label: Ember Hill

title: Harvest Weight
description: Originals rather than traditionals this time, and strong enough that most listeners cannot tell which is which. Plainly sung and beautifully played.
label: Ember Hill

title: Northern Line Soul
description: British soul with a horn section that could hold its own anywhere. Ignored at home on release and heavily bootlegged everywhere else.
label: Quarry Bank Sound

title: Vance!
description: Recorded live in front of two hundred people who plainly knew every word. The best possible argument for his back catalogue.
label: Quarry Bank Sound

title: Dub in the Mailroom
description: The studio band stepping out from behind everyone else's singles. Instrumental, spacious and mixed with obvious glee.
label: Silver Fathom

title: Return Postage
description: Heavier and stranger than the first, with the desk treated as the lead instrument throughout. A dub record in the proper sense.
label: Silver Fathom

title: Small Hours, Long Roads
description: Songs other people made famous, here in their original and considerably bleaker form. The definitive versions by some distance.
label: Cormorant Records

title: Ashes in the Yard
description: Afrobeat-inflected funk with a horn section that refuses to stop for breath. Three tracks, one side each, no filler anywhere.
label: Coastal Union

title: Market Day
description: Looser than the debut and considerably more percussive. Reissued in 2014 and gone from our shelves within a fortnight.
label: Coastal Union

title: Wired Up Wrong
description: Electric blues recorded cheap and fast with the amplifier complaining audibly throughout. That complaint is most of the appeal.
label: Foundry Street

title: South Side Standard
description: A band record rather than a solo one, with a rhythm section that pushes him somewhere new. Underrated then and now.
label: Foundry Street

title: Transit Signal
description: The debut, recorded in a fortnight for almost nothing, and still the coldest thing in their catalogue. Post-punk with the shouting removed.
label: Northbound Sound

title: Hot Plate Sessions
description: The house band finally billed on their own sleeve, playing the material they had been sharpening behind other singers for years.
label: Trestle Records

title: Every Night This Week
description: Live to two-track in a club they played most weeks, with all the between-song noise left in. As close to being there as vinyl manages.
label: Trestle Records

title: Rivers of Sound
description: Roots singing of the sort that defined the decade, with arrangements that leave enormous amounts of room. A cornerstone record.
label: Silver Fathom

title: Rivers in Dub
description: The companion dub to Rivers of Sound, taken apart by the same band that built it. Arguably the better of the two records.
label: Silver Fathom

title: Hold the Line Steady
description: Gospel phrasing applied to secular material, delivered with enough authority to settle any argument about the difference.
label: Nightpost Records

title: Alma Live at the Regent
description: One night, one reel, no edits. The band are excellent and she is plainly on a different plane entirely.
label: Nightpost Records

title: Kansas City Jump
description: Dance hall blues by a trio who spent decades playing for people who wanted to move. Cheerful, brisk and completely without ego.
label: Waypoint Audio

title: Last of the Front Rooms
description: Late sides cut in the houses of friends, with conversation audible between takes. The last recordings he made and among the best.
label: Waypoint Audio

title: Noite Comprida
description: Darker and more orchestral than her sixties work, recorded after a five-year silence. Worth the wait and then some.
label: Verdant Sound

title: Ritmo del Puerto
description: The orchestra's last great session before the personnel scattered. Enormous, joyful and recorded far better than it needed to be.
label: Coastal Union

title: Cold Frequencies
description: The second album, and the one where the drum sound arrived. Widely imitated since, rarely equalled.
label: Northbound Sound

title: The Glass Corridor
description: Synthesisers pushed to the front and the guitars used as texture. Divided the audience on release and looks obviously correct now.
label: Northbound Sound

title: Interior Weather
description: The fourth record, quietly the best, and the one nobody bought at the time. Start here if you want the argument settled.
label: Northbound Sound

title: Harbour Lights
description: Choruses built for rooms with balconies, delivered by a band who had never played one at the time. They would soon enough.
label: Quarry Bank Sound

title: Every Town Has One
description: Their commercial peak, and unusually for such things, also their best set of songs. The production has aged more gracefully than most.
label: Quarry Bank Sound

title: Winter Pier
description: Recorded as the band were falling apart and all the better for the tension. A proper closing statement, intentional or otherwise.
label: Quarry Bank Sound

title: Paper Hearts
description: Twelve songs, none over three minutes, not one of them wasted. The template a great many bands have since worked from.
label: Gable End

title: Second Class Post
description: Jangling, bittersweet and recorded in three weeks flat. The singles are famous and the album tracks are better.
label: Gable End

title: The Last Word
description: Their farewell record, made without anyone announcing it as one. Sadder and sharper than anything else they did.
label: Gable End

title: Kentish Town Nights
description: The debut, written entirely in a shared flat on the road they took their name from. Modest ambitions, immodestly good songs.
label: Lowtide Recordings

title: Streetlight Economy
description: Bigger production, same songwriting, and the point at which people outside London started paying attention.
label: Lowtide Recordings

title: The Ferry Home
description: Traditional tunes and new writing sequenced so you cannot tell where one ends. Recorded quickly because the band were bored of studios.
label: Ember Hill

title: Salt and Rope
description: Their most-played record in this shop, largely because it never lets up. Fiddle-led, fast and completely unsentimental.
label: Ember Hill

title: Late Rehearsal
description: Standards taken apart with obvious affection and reassembled slightly wrong. Her first record and already fully formed.
label: Blue Meridian

title: Second Language
description: Originals for the first time, sung with the same liberties she takes with everyone else's material. Quietly one of the decade's best vocal jazz records.
label: Blue Meridian

title: Vals para Nadie
description: Tango played by people who grew up with it and refuse to treat it as a museum piece. Elegant and just slightly unstable.
label: Verdant Sound

title: Puerto Gris
description: The record where the jazz players in the group stopped pretending otherwise. Freer, stranger and thoroughly recommended.
label: Verdant Sound

title: Basement Pressure
description: UK dub built on a desk held together with tape and optimism. Enormous low end and an unusual amount of wit.
label: Silver Fathom

title: Committee Rules
description: Drum machines folded into the mix without losing an ounce of weight. A bridge between two scenes that mostly ignored each other.
label: Silver Fathom

title: Quartets, Volume One
description: Familiar repertoire taken at unfamiliar tempos, which annoyed a great many people and delighted the rest. Superbly recorded.
label: Harrow Lane Records

title: Night Pieces
description: A programme of quieter works played with the same argumentative streak. The most approachable thing in their catalogue.
label: Harrow Lane Records

title: Concrete Gardens
description: Made with borrowed samplers and a great deal of nerve. Still turning up in other people's sets three decades later.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Municipal Dreams
description: Warmer than the debut and considerably more melodic, without giving up any of the strangeness. An easy first purchase.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Golden City Sessions
description: Township jazz, funk and something else entirely, held together by one of the great bass players. Generous, warm music.
label: Coastal Union

title: Long Way from the Coast
description: A larger band and a bigger sound, recorded in two cities and sequenced as one continuous set. His most confident record.
label: Coastal Union

title: First Editions
description: The debut, built from records the crew grew up with and dubbed onto tape long before anyone bought it. Foundational stuff.
label: Foundry Street

title: Overture and Interval
description: Concert arrangements of theatre music, recorded because the orchestra kept being asked to play it live. More fun than that sounds.
label: Harrow Lane Records

title: The Antwerp Tapes
description: Home recordings from a fallow decade, released years later once someone found the reels. Rough, intimate and essential.
label: Cormorant Records

title: Nothing Doing
description: Arrived at the end of a scene they were never really part of, which cost them then and looks like foresight now. Restrained where their peers were not.
label: Lowtide Recordings

title: The Slow Part
description: Quieter, longer and considerably better than the debut. The record their reputation was eventually rebuilt on.
label: Lowtide Recordings

title: Ordnance Survey
description: Guitar music with an unusual amount of care taken over the words. Should have been enormous and somehow never was.
label: Northbound Sound

title: Second City Fiction
description: Recorded after their label lost interest, which freed them up entirely. The best thing they ever did by a comfortable margin.
label: Northbound Sound

title: Common Ground
description: The band at full stretch, with arrangements that finally match the ambition of the songwriting. Their most durable record.
label: Lowtide Recordings

title: Terminus
description: A closing statement recorded with no expectation of a follow-up. Sombre, generous and completely unhurried.
label: Lowtide Recordings

title: Second Editions
description: Denser and funnier than the debut, built on samples that would be unclearable today. A golden-age record in the truest sense.
label: Foundry Street

title: Borough Business
description: Live instrumentation folded in beside the breaks, years before that became the obvious move. Warm and unusually spacious.
label: Foundry Street

title: Press Run
description: Their last record together and the one that sounds least like a farewell. Confident, loose and plainly enjoying itself.
label: Foundry Street

title: Local Frequencies
description: British hip-hop with no interest in sounding like anywhere else, full of place names you would need a map for. All the better for it.
label: Quarry Bank Sound

title: Night Bus Radio
description: Recorded almost entirely between midnight and dawn and sequenced to be heard the same way. Their best-loved record.
label: Quarry Bank Sound

title: Assembly Line
description: Machine music made by people who were present at the beginning and never got precious about it. Warm where you expect cold.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Third Shift
description: Longer tracks, deeper mixes and a marked drop in tempo. Built for the very end of the night rather than the middle of it.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Public Works
description: The most sample-heavy record in their catalogue, assembled from sources nobody has ever fully identified. Endlessly replayable.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Low Orbit
description: Beatless for long stretches and none the worse for it. The record the ambient crowd claimed and the dance crowd never quite forgave.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Signal Decay
description: A debut assembled alone over four years on borrowed hardware. Restless, precise and entirely without filler.
label: Meridian Tapes

title: Harbour Static
description: Field recordings and drum programming in roughly equal measure. Considerably warmer than the title suggests.
label: Meridian Tapes

title: Postcards from the Boulevard
description: Synthetic, bright and hiding real melancholy under the gloss. A record that gets sadder the better you know it.
label: Gable End

title: Everything in Neon
description: The hits record that was not a hits record, made of new songs written to sound familiar. A neat trick, well executed.
label: Gable End

title: The Long Meadow
description: Traditional playing with a songwriter's ear, recorded live in a village hall over two afternoons. Nothing here is showing off.
label: Ember Hill

title: Winter Ground
description: Sparser and darker than what came before, with the guitar mixed close enough to hear the room. A grower, and a considerable one.
label: Ember Hill

title: Preludes, Live in Budapest
description: Recorded in concert with the audience audible and the occasional fumble left in. Far more alive than a studio take would have been.
label: Harrow Lane Records

title: Late Sonatas
description: Big, serious repertoire played without a hint of reverence. The interpretations are arguable and that is rather the point.
label: Harrow Lane Records

title: Room for Everything
description: A bassist's record in the best sense, where the low end leads and everyone else responds. Light on its feet throughout.
label: Blue Meridian

title: Long Endings
description: Exactly what the title promises, with three tracks that take their time dissolving. Ideal late-evening listening.
label: Blue Meridian

title: Kitchen Table Sessions
description: Neo-soul with the polish deliberately left off and the drums pushed forward. Her debut and still the most direct thing she has made.
label: Trestle Records

title: Sahel Blues
description: Desert blues that trades urgency for hypnosis and wins the exchange comfortably. Recorded in two days with almost no overdubs.
label: Coastal Union

title: Score for a Quiet Film
description: A score that works without the picture, which is the highest compliment available. Sparse writing with enormous patience behind it.
label: Lantern Row

title: Northern Light
description: Written for a documentary nobody saw and reissued on its own merits. Strings, silence and very little else.
label: Lantern Row

title: Southbound Nothing
description: A debut that arrived a couple of years after it would have been fashionable, and is much better for having missed.
label: Ash & Iron Records

title: Milonga Nueva
description: The trio's return after a long silence, with a younger bandoneon player who changes the balance entirely. Sharper and less nostalgic.
label: Verdant Sound

title: Ciudad Doble
description: Two long suites recorded either side of a European tour. Their most adventurous work and their least played, unfairly.
label: Verdant Sound

title: The Slow Reveal
description: Bigger, slower and considerably more confident than the debut. The record that turned a cult following into a real one.
label: Ash & Iron Records

title: Under the Overpass
description: Recorded in a single room with the band facing each other and almost nothing fixed afterwards. Rough in all the right places.
label: Ash & Iron Records

title: Tidal Range
description: Guitar music that unfolds at its own pace and refuses to be rushed by anyone. Six tracks, forty-eight minutes, no complaints.
label: Lowtide Recordings

title: Estuary
description: Quieter and more textural than the debut, recorded largely at dawn because the studio was cheaper. It shows, helpfully.
label: Lowtide Recordings

title: Return to Sender
description: Wiry, sharp-elbowed guitar music with lyrics worth reading on their own. Their debut and their most immediate record.
label: Cormorant Records

title: No Forwarding Address
description: Made during the first of their two break-ups, which you can hear throughout. Tense, brilliant and slightly unpleasant.
label: Cormorant Records

title: Late Editions
description: A reunion record made with no fanfare and no expectations whatsoever. Considerably better than reunion records are entitled to be.
label: Northbound Sound

title: North of the Border
description: Sequenced by DJs, which is why it works best played end to end and loudly. Nothing here is in the wrong order.
label: Waypoint Audio

title: Common Tongue
description: Their most political record and their most tuneful, which is not the usual pairing. Ages remarkably well.
label: Quarry Bank Sound

title: Last Orders
description: Live horns, live drums and a crew who had clearly stopped caring what anyone expected. A generous, celebratory record.
label: Quarry Bank Sound

title: Long Form One
description: Two pieces, one per side, both unhurried in the extreme. Exactly what the collective's name promises and no less welcome for it.
label: Meridian Tapes

title: Grain and Tape
description: Built almost entirely from degraded tape loops and left deliberately unpolished. The most tactile record in this section.
label: Meridian Tapes

title: Before the Peak
description: Dance music for the hours either side of the main event, made by a duo with no interest in the main event. Patient and beautifully mixed.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Empty Room Theory
description: Sparse to the point of austerity and never once cold. A debut that arrived fully formed, which is unusual and slightly annoying.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Between Two Silences
description: Solo piano recorded in an empty hall with the sustain pedal doing much of the arranging. Almost nothing here is hurried.
label: Blue Meridian

title: The Space Between Notes
description: A trio record for once, though she still leaves more room than most players would dare. Our most reliable jazz recommendation.
label: Blue Meridian

title: Highlife Studies
description: Post-bop structures with highlife phrasing folded in so naturally you stop noticing the join. A remarkable debut.
label: Coastal Union

title: Full Arrangement
description: A big band that nobody could afford, playing charts written out in full. Impossibly tight and audibly delighted about it.
label: Trestle Records

title: Committee Business
description: Recorded live in two nights with a horn section of eleven. The room noise is half the record and entirely welcome.
label: Trestle Records

title: Heavy Rotation
description: Bigger production than the debut without losing the grit that made it work. Her most-played record in this shop.
label: Trestle Records

title: The Tuesday Set
description: Songs worked out in public during a weekly residency and recorded once they were ready. Sounds like a room, which is rare now.
label: Gable End

title: Residency
description: More assured and slightly sadder, with arrangements that make room for a proper string section. Their high point so far.
label: Gable End

title: Dust Road
description: Country music played by people who plainly love it rather than wearing it. Harmonies first, everything else afterwards.
label: Ember Hill

title: River Crossing
description: A band record after two solo ones, with percussion that changes the whole centre of gravity. Hypnotic in a different way.
label: Coastal Union

title: Music for a Border Town
description: Written for a film few people saw and sold steadily ever since to people who never will. Works entirely on its own terms.
label: Lantern Row

title: Two Winters
description: Two scores collected on one record, sharing a mood and almost nothing else. The second half is the reason to buy it.
label: Lantern Row

title: The Cartographer
description: Synthesisers alongside the strings for the first time, used sparingly and to real effect. His most-played score by some distance.
label: Lantern Row

title: Tango de Aeropuerto
description: Written almost entirely in transit and recorded in a fortnight at home. Restless music that never settles, deliberately.
label: Verdant Sound

title: Cold Water Swimming
description: Recorded in a converted fish processing plant on the coast, which you can hear in every reverb tail. Glacial and quietly enormous.
label: Northbound Sound

title: The Slow Thaw
description: Warmer than the debut without giving up any of the patience. Four of these six tracks pass eight minutes and none outstay their welcome.
label: Northbound Sound

title: Low Tide Radio
description: Reverb-soaked guitar music built for headphones and long journeys. The record that made the band's reputation outside their own city.
label: Lowtide Recordings

title: Static & Sea
description: Synthesisers used as weather rather than melody, layered under the guitars until you stop separating them. Their most immersive record.
label: Lowtide Recordings

title: Every Quiet Thing
description: Songs that begin almost apologetically and end somewhere considerably louder. A debut that finally caught up with a live reputation.
label: Cormorant Records

title: House on Fire
description: Recorded fast with a full band and almost nothing repaired afterwards. The most direct thing in her catalogue.
label: Cormorant Records

title: Corridor Six
description: Written and mostly recorded overnight in a rehearsal room above a motorway services. Widescreen rock made in a very small space.
label: Ash & Iron Records

title: Service Station Hymns
description: Bigger in every dimension than the debut and still recognisably the same band. The choruses are the point and they know it.
label: Ash & Iron Records

title: Signal Fires
description: Recorded almost entirely alone in a flat in Hamburg, then toured with a band twice the size. The homemade intimacy survives the volume.
label: Cormorant Records

title: Ground Sea
description: Arrived with no announcement four years after anyone expected it, and stayed in rotation for a decade. Tidal in the truest sense.
label: Lowtide Recordings

title: Dead Letter Club
description: The self-titled reunion record made after their first break-up. Sharper and considerably more generous than what preceded it.
label: Cormorant Records

title: Interference Pattern
description: A debut that arrived fully assembled, loud and unusually good at knowing when to stop. The most asked-about band on this wall.
label: Northbound Sound

title: Residency Hours
description: Written for the club she was playing four nights a week and recorded in the same room. Music built for a specific space and it travels anyway.
label: Blue Meridian

title: Halflight
description: A collaboration that had no business working, folding Voss's production instincts into Marsh's writing. It works completely.
label: Blue Meridian

title: Loop and Horn
description: Jazz arranged like a dance record, with the structure doing most of the emotional work. Stranger and better than it sounds on paper.
label: Meridian Tapes

title: The Accra Sessions
description: Recorded at home with local players rather than an imported band, which changes everything about how it breathes.
label: Coastal Union

title: Coastal Path
description: Assembled from tape of actual places and processed until the places are only a rumour. Best heard walking.
label: Meridian Tapes

title: Weather Station
description: Longer and less forgiving than the debut, built around a single recording made over eleven months. Genuinely immersive.
label: Meridian Tapes

title: After Hours Protocol
description: Dance music with the urgency removed and the texture doubled. Built for a proper system and slightly wasted on anything else.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Second Room
description: Named for the smaller room at the club, which tells you exactly what it is for. Patient, warm and beautifully sequenced.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Negative Space
description: Even sparser than the debut, which seemed impossible at the time. What is missing carries as much as what is there.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Ashwood
description: Acoustic guitar and field recordings folded into the usual machinery, to genuinely disorienting effect. The outlier in her catalogue.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Tessellate
description: Precise, restless and constitutionally unable to sit still. Changes direction roughly every ninety seconds and gets away with it.
label: Waypoint Audio

title: Sunday Best
description: Immaculate pop songs sung with just enough weariness to keep them from cloying. A debut with no wasted seconds.
label: Gable End

title: Occasion Wear
description: Glossier and sadder, with arrangements that reward the volume being turned up. Their best set of choruses so far.
label: Gable End

title: Small Hours
description: Written, played and produced alone, which is exactly why it sounds like nobody else. Bright on the surface, bleak underneath.
label: Nightpost Records

title: Paper Weather
description: More electronic and more direct, with three of the sharpest songs she has written. A short record that does not waste a second.
label: Nightpost Records

title: Long Paragraphs
description: Dense writing delivered like conversation, over beats that leave plenty of room for it. Rewards a fourth listen and survives the first.
label: Foundry Street

title: Second Person
description: Live musicians throughout and a noticeably lighter touch. His most musical record and probably his best.
label: Foundry Street

title: Marges Lucides
description: Two languages treated as two instruments, over jazz-leaning beats with a real editor's discipline. Nothing here is longer than it needs to be.
label: Waypoint Audio

title: Compás Roto
description: Flamenco training applied to songs that are not flamenco, with the rhythmic discipline fully intact. Stark and hypnotic.
label: Verdant Sound

title: Tierra Seca
description: A fuller band and a wider palette without losing the severity that made the debut work. Her most complete record.
label: Verdant Sound

title: Family Business
description: Harmonies stacked four deep over songs that would work with none at all. Country music with real craft under the warmth.
label: Ember Hill

title: Bridgetown Roots
description: Modern roots singing with a producer's ear for space. Patient in a way that new reggae records rarely bother being.
label: Silver Fathom

title: Short Fuse
description: Slide guitar played with punk impatience, no track over three minutes and no solos for the sake of it. Refreshing and slightly rude.
label: Foundry Street

title: The Gilded Curtain
description: The original cast recording, made across two days with the pit orchestra fully live in the room. Far better recorded than most of its kind.
label: Lantern Row

title: The Quiet Coast
description: A television score collected as an album and much the better for the edit. Strings, patience and a very light hand.
label: Lantern Row

title: Northern Crossing
description: Her most expansive score to date, written for a series that ran three seasons. Works perfectly well without any of them.
label: Lantern Row

title: Bad Reception
description: Louder and angrier than the debut, recorded in nine days with almost nothing fixed afterwards. A proper second record.
label: Northbound Sound

title: Standing Wave
description: The record where the band stopped shouting and became considerably more frightening. Their best work by a distance.
label: Northbound Sound

title: Nightshift
description: Written on tour and recorded immediately afterwards, which accounts for both the fatigue and the momentum. Their most direct album.
label: Ash & Iron Records

title: Weathervane
description: Four years in the making and audibly worth it, with strings on half the tracks and no loss of nerve. A genuine step up.
label: Ash & Iron Records

title: Concrete Bloom
description: Her heaviest record, made with a rhythm section she had been touring with for years. Nothing tentative anywhere on it.
label: Cormorant Records

title: Slow Burn Season
description: Acoustic for long stretches and all the more forceful for it. The most recent thing on this wall and already a staff favourite.
label: Cormorant Records

title: Distant Early Warning
description: The guitars pushed back and the drums pushed forward, which changes the band entirely. Divisive and completely convincing.
label: Lowtide Recordings

title: Meltwater
description: Recorded across two winters in the same converted plant as the debut. Slower, warmer and considerably more melodic.
label: Northbound Sound

title: Hamburg Tapes
description: Back to recording alone after two band albums, and the songs benefit enormously from the smaller room.
label: Cormorant Records

title: Half-Light Hours
description: Club tracks with an unusual amount of sadness built into them. A debut that sold out three pressings before anyone noticed.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Lisbon After Rain
description: Slower, longer and more melodic than the debut, and considerably harder to keep in stock. Genuinely special.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Nine Figures
description: As restless as ever but rather better arranged, with three tracks that finally hold still long enough to land.
label: Waypoint Audio

title: Recursive
description: Built from a single motif taken apart across seven tracks. Their most conceptual record and, unexpectedly, their most danceable.
label: Waypoint Audio

title: Ice Road
description: Recorded across a single winter journey and processed for two years afterwards. Bleak, beautiful and very long.
label: Meridian Tapes

title: Closing Time Signature
description: Exactly what the duo have always done, done better than they have done it before. For the very end of the night.
label: Pressing Room 4

title: Sparrow
description: Very small sounds arranged around very large hooks. A debut that seemed slight on release and has not stopped growing since.
label: Nightpost Records

title: Second Flight
description: The record that made everyone pay proper attention, built on the same principles at three times the scale.
label: Nightpost Records

title: Common Weather
description: Her first record made with an outside producer, and the collaboration is plainly good for her. Sharper and warmer at once.
label: Nightpost Records

title: The Understudy
description: Written across a year off and recorded in three weeks. Quiet, exact and among the best things released this year.
label: Nightpost Records

title: Best Behaviour
description: Sunnier than anything they have made and hiding just as much underneath. The choruses do a great deal of quiet work.
label: Gable End

title: Low Country
description: Slow, heavy and mixed so the low end genuinely matters. The newest name in this section and already the most requested.
label: Foundry Street

title: Third Person
description: Completes a loose trilogy and is comfortably the most assured part of it. Live band, long verses, no filler.
label: Foundry Street

title: Notes in the Margin
description: Recorded with a jazz trio in the room, which turns out to be exactly what these songs wanted. Elegant and unusually short.
label: Waypoint Audio

title: Night Kitchen
description: Written during a year with no gigs and recorded the moment there were rooms to play again. You can hear the relief.
label: Blue Meridian

title: Standard Time
description: Her first standards record, approached with the same appetite for rearrangement she brings to her own material.
label: Blue Meridian

title: Machine Ballads
description: Loops, horns and an unusual amount of tenderness. The clearest statement yet of what she has been working towards.
label: Meridian Tapes

title: Osaka Solo
description: Back to solo piano in a hall she has recorded in three times before. As spare and as generous as anything in her catalogue.
label: Blue Meridian

title: Salt Air Dub
description: A full dub companion to her second album, mixed by the singer herself. Heavier and stranger than the vocal versions.
label: Silver Fathom

title: Steady Ground
description: Horns, harmonies and a rhythm section with nothing to prove. The most joyful record she has made.
label: Silver Fathom

title: Bottleneck
description: Eleven songs in twenty-nine minutes, played like she has somewhere to be. The impatience remains the whole appeal.
label: Foundry Street

title: Casa Vacía
description: Recorded in an empty house over one summer with two microphones. The most intimate thing she has released.
label: Verdant Sound

title: Long Way Home
description: Their first record in six years and their warmest, with a couple of the best songs anyone in this section wrote last year.
label: Ember Hill

title: The Cartographer's Daughter
description: A score written for a film that was never finished, released on its own terms instead. Complete in every way that matters.
label: Lantern Row

title: Nocturnes, Revisited
description: A return to repertoire she first recorded thirty years ago, taken slower and with far less to prove. Remarkable playing.
label: Harrow Lane Records
